objective: Read-only characterize generic GitHub Actions trigger/write isolation on stable main and identify candidate-agnostic static policy gaps that could permit accidental result-bearing retrigger or cross-purpose mutation.
finding_summary: Stable main contains seven GitHub Actions workflows. Ordinary CI is broadly push/PR triggered but non-mutating; authoritative tag creation and the default-branch formal registration guard are manually dispatched and strongly fail-closed.

Three workflows combine main-push path triggers with elevated capability: a harmless dispatch-capability probe, the legacy CX01 one-way launch bridge with actions+contents write, and the legacy CX01 evidence-preservation bridge with contents write.

The launch and preservation bridges have strong exact-binding/no-clobber internal guards, but workflow-definition edits still automatically enter write-capable control paths; operation-level safety is stronger than trigger-level isolation.

Both historical scientific bridges are currently self-disarmed: the durable STARTED/control branch and durable preservation branch already exist, so their explicit branch-absence checks should fail before replay/recreation.

A reusable candidate-agnostic static policy/linter could prohibit automatic push/PR triggers from coexisting with elevated actions/contents write plus workflow-dispatch or control/preserve/formal/evidence ref-writing semantics, absent an explicit reviewed exception.
